title: The Letter of Ashcombe
premise: When the coffin of Ashcombe's founder, Edmund Ashcombe, is exhumed for a cemetery relocation and found empty, night-shift taxi dispatcher Gideon Blackwood — who knows every route, secret, and skeleton in the town — is hired by the founder's estranged granddaughter to find out what happened. Gideon discovers that thirty years ago a cab driver named Ruth Okafor vanished the same week Edmund supposedly died, and that the town's founding families conspired to bury one story inside another. Following dispatch logs, a hidden letter, and Ruth's surviving daughter, Gideon uncovers that Edmund faked his death to escape his partners' crimes and lived out his days as Ruth's quiet benefactor before dying in obscurity. The climax comes when the last living conspirator tries to burn the evidence and Gideon must choose between exposing a lie that holds the town together or letting Ashcombe keep its myth; Gideon chooses truth, and the town — and Gideon's own sense of belonging — is remade by it.
about_author: Felix Vasquez spent a decade working overnight shifts in small-town radio before turning to crime fiction, a background that gives his novels their intimate knowledge of who is awake at 3 a.m. He lives in coastal New England, where he collects antique ledgers and insists every mystery he writes could plausibly be solved from behind a desk.

chapters.title: The Empty Box
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Gideon Blackwood, mid-shift, when news breaks that Edmund Ashcombe's exhumed coffin contains nothing but river stones. The town erupts; Gideon, professionally unbothered, takes a call from Vera Ashcombe asking to hire them. Emotional beat: curiosity sharpening into unease as Gideon realizes the stones are local — someone from Ashcombe did this.

chapters.title: Dispatch Rules
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV establishes their method: they solve cases through cab records, radio chatter, and knowing where everyone was. They pull thirty-year-old dispatch logs and find a gap — three nights erased around Edmund's death. Beat: confidence undercut by the first sign someone has been here before, cutting pages out.

chapters.title: The Granddaughter
chapters.summary: Vera Ashcombe explains her motive: her grandfather left her nothing but a sealed letter she can't open until 'the truth of him' is settled. Gideon agrees to take the case. Beat: wary alliance formed; Gideon notices Vera grieves a man she never met, and recognizes the hunger for belonging.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: Gideon interviews the old guard — the mayor, the funeral director, the retired police chief — whose alibis for the death week are suspiciously identical, word for word. Beat: dread builds as Gideon maps how rehearsed the town's memory is; someone taught Ashcombe what to remember.

chapters.title: The Driver Who Vanished
chapters.summary: Digging into the excised log nights, Gideon finds Ruth Okafor, a cab driver who disappeared the same week Edmund died, leaving a young daughter. The town remembers her vaguely, unkindly. Beat: grief and anger; Gideon realizes two mysteries were buried in one grave.

chapters.title: River Stones
chapters.summary: Gideon traces the stones filling the coffin to a specific quarry load sold thirty years ago — bought by the funeral director, paid with an account tied to the founding families. Beat: the conspiracy gains shape; Gideon feels watched for the first time, headlights idling outside their apartment.

chapters.title: What the Radio Heard
chapters.summary: A retired dispatcher, half-lucid, recalls the night Ruth vanished: a fare to the quarry road, then silence, then orders from above to log nothing. Beat: horror crystallizes — the cover-up ran through Gideon's own profession, implicating the chair they sit in.

chapters.title: The Letter's Seal
chapters.summary: Vera, impatient, nearly breaks her grandfather's seal early; Gideon stops her, arguing the letter only means something once its context is proven. Their alliance strains. Beat: tension between truth-now and truth-complete; Gideon admits, privately, why unfinished cases haunt them — their own missing parent.

chapters.title: Ashcombe House
chapters.summary: Breaking into the shuttered Ashcombe estate, Gideon finds Edmund's study preserved like a shrine — and a second ledger matching the cab company's, in Edmund's hand, recording fares he took under a false name after his 'death.' Beat: vertigo; the dead man was alive, driving his own town's streets.

chapters.title: The Man Called Wren
chapters.summary: Following the alias 'Wren' through old records, Gideon finds rent receipts, a fishing license, a photograph: Edmund lived twenty years nearby, poor and anonymous. Someone sheltered him. Beat: wonder complicating suspicion — the fraud had a conscience, or a keeper.

chapters.title: Ruth's Daughter
chapters.summary: Gideon locates Amara Okafor, raised by an aunt, told her mother abandoned her. She keeps a box of Ruth's things, including a letter from 'E.A.' promising money and protection. Beat: fury and tenderness collide; Amara wants nothing from Ashcombe, and Gideon understands belonging can be a wound.

chapters.title: The Partners
chapters.summary: Gideon reconstructs the founding trio: Edmund, Harlan Voss, and Cecily Marsh, whose fortunes built the town on a land deal that required Ruth's silence — she'd driven them to a meeting where a fourth partner died. Beat: the motive lands with weight; the town itself is built on the buried night.

chapters.title: Threats at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Anonymous calls come through Gideon's own dispatch line — a voice reciting Gideon's parentage, implying they don't belong in Ashcombe either. Beat: fear turns personal; the case has found the soft place in Gideon and pressed down.

chapters.title: Cecily Marsh Confesses Nothing
chapters.summary: The last living partner, ancient and sharp, receives Gideon and admits nothing while confirming everything, insisting the lie saved the town from ruin. Beat: moral vertigo — Cecily is monstrous and persuasive, and Gideon wavers for the first time.

chapters.title: The Quarry Road
chapters.summary: Gideon walks the quarry road at night, reconstructing Ruth's final drive, and finds the old foundation of a cabin — Edmund's refuge — with a loose stone hiding letters between Edmund and Ruth. Beat: heartbreak; Ruth didn't vanish, she was killed for knowing, and Edmund spent his life paying a debt he couldn't speak.

chapters.title: What Edmund Wrote
chapters.summary: The letters reveal everything: the accidental death, the pact, Ruth's murder by Voss to secure silence, Edmund's exile-in-plain-sight, and his instruction that the truth surface only when no conspirator could bury it again. Beat: solemnity; Gideon now carries the whole weight of the town's founding lie.

chapters.title: Vera Decides
chapters.summary: Gideon tells Vera everything; she opens her letter at last — Edmund's apology and confession, naming Voss and Marsh. Vera must choose between her name and the truth. Beat: catharsis and resolve; Vera chooses truth, mirroring Gideon's own coming choice.

chapters.title: Fire at the Archive
chapters.summary: Someone torches the county archive where Gideon deposited copies; the dispatcher's office is ransacked, the old logs gone. Only the quarry letters survive, hidden on Gideon's body. Beat: escalation to crisis; the enemy is cornered and burning the past faster than Gideon can prove it.

chapters.title: Harlan's Son
chapters.summary: Gideon confronts Daniel Voss, who has spent his life protecting his father's name and orchestrated the threats and fires. In a standoff at the quarry, Daniel nearly forces Gideon off the edge. Beat: physical climax; Gideon survives by doing what they do best — knowing the ground, the roads, the dark.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: At a packed town meeting, Vera reads Edmund's letter aloud and Gideon presents the quarry correspondence. Cecily, dying, confirms it all. Ashcombe shatters and reassembles around the truth. Beat: public reckoning; the town's identity is rewritten in real time.

chapters.title: Ruth's Grave
chapters.summary: Ruth Okafor is reburied with her name spoken plainly, beside a new marker for Edmund, who asked in his letters to be buried near her. Amara and Vera stand together, strangers made family. Beat: mourning turned to belonging; inheritance redefined as truth passed down.

chapters.title: Night Shift
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Gideon returns to the dispatch desk, the town quieter and more honest. A new caller asks for help finding a missing person, and Gideon takes the case. Beat: resolution and renewal; Gideon finally belongs to Ashcombe not by blood or myth, but by having carried its truth.
